About the Role:

We are seeking a Program Manager to support the Energy and Sustainability organization’s clean energy strategy and the reporting that underpins Net Zero commitments.
The role will serve as the day-to-day owner and coordinator for energy activity data — the Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 energy datasets that feed the company's greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory, emissions forecasting, and voluntary and regulatory disclosures.
This is a hands-on, data-centric role requiring 3-5 years of experience managing multiple concurrent workstreams in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, direct experience working with large datasets and running or Quality Checking (QC'ing) analytics, and the ability to communicate data status and insights to technical and non-technical audiences.
The individual must have familiarity with corporate GHG accounting and be comfortable with query tools and data Quality Assurance (QA)/validation workflows.

Job Title:
Sustainability Program Manager II
Minimum Qualifications:

BA or BS degree in physical sciences, engineering, math, statistics, accounting, business, environment, and/or a sustainability-focused field.
3-5 years of experience in program management, data operations, or analytics coordination, ideally supporting technical or data-oriented teams.
Direct, hands-on experience working with large datasets — collecting, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), reconciling, and analyzing data from multiple sources.
Familiarity with corporate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions accounting concepts (Scope 1, 2, and 3) and the activity data that underpins an emissions inventory.
Exceptional project-management skills with a demonstrated ability to self-manage complex, data-driven delivery in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting data and insights to technical and non-technical audiences and creating graphics for leadership presentations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data work, even under tight deadlines.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with a scripting/query language (e.g., Structured Query Language (SQL), Python) sufficient to run, automate, or Quality Assurance (QA) data pulls from large data warehouses (e.g., Hive/Presto or equivalent).
Experience building visualizations and dashboards from large, multi-source datasets, particularly with Tableau and Excel.
Familiarity with energy/utility data (electricity, natural gas, diesel, and other fuels) and metering/billing data structures.
Strong understanding of current practices and trends in greenhouse gas emissions and broader sustainability accounting and reporting.
Familiarity with external reporting standards and platforms such as Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP), Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), etc.
Experience supporting external assurance or audit processes.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as the day-to-day owner for energy activity data across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 electricity (e.g., FERA, construction energy, network-related electricity, and operational electricity, diesel, natural gas, etc.), from data collection and Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) through to the reporting handoff to the Net Zero team.
Perform analyses on the Environmental Attribute Certificate (EAC) portfolio and support the development of internal systems to advance portfolio management and modeling.
Run and maintain the recurring data collection, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), and validation cadence (e.g., quarterly data pulls, follow-ups, Year-over-Year (YoY) analysis) and keep reporting and analysis on schedule.
Perform and Quality Check (QC) data pulls from energy data systems, investigate anomalies and data-pipeline issues, and reconcile discrepancies.
Coordinate data and process flows across cross-functional partners to maintain accurate and complete inputs from source through to reporting.
Support the emissions forecasting cadence as the energy-data point of contact for the Net Zero team, providing and Quality Assuring (QA'ing) the activity data behind regulatory and internal cross-functional forecasts.
Develop and maintain program-management artifacts — trackers, roadmaps, status reports, and executive-ready updates — for recurring leadership and cross-functional forums.
Support a quarterly reporting cadence (execution updates, executive meeting preparation, deck and dashboard creation) using established templates and inputs.
Support external assurance and audit activities (e.g., methodology walkthroughs with the assurance provider) and prepare and validate data and documentation as requested.
Triage and respond to incoming energy-data and analytical requests; track progress against internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and stakeholder expectations.
Maintain and improve reporting documentation — the what, when, where, how, and why of energy data collection, including team-specific nuances and process flows.

Location:
 Remote [USA ONLY]

The salary for this position is between $116,400 - $166,400 annually.  Factors which may affect pay within this range may include geography/market, skills, education, experience, and other qualifications of the successful candidate.

jobs.title: Principal Program Manager - OCI Product Marketing
jobs.description:
Job Description

We are looking for a strategic Program Manager (IC4)
to establish and run the operating model for business-critical OCI Web and Oracle AI World
programs. This role brings sustained cross-functional coordination, clear governance, and operational rigor to high-visibility initiatives that require consistent execution across Product Marketing, Product Management, Web Publishing, Website Builder (WSB), Corporate Marketing, and executive stakeholders.

You will own the program mechanisms that make complex work move: priorities, dependencies, readiness criteria, status reporting, risk escalation, stakeholder alignment, and adoption. You thrive in ambiguity, build consensus across diverse teams, and create practical processes that scale.

Responsibilities

OCI Website Migration to Website Builder (WSB)

Drive migration readiness, validation, prioritization, and issue resolution across the OCI website portfolio, including 239 product and solution pages on oracle.com/cloud and the assessment of a further 183 AI pages.
Coordinate dependencies across WSB, Web Publishing, Product Marketing, Product Management, page owners, and reviewers to maintain a clear migration plan and timely decisions.
Manage the reversion and remigration path for OCI pages previously moved to non-compatible page template, ensuring page quality, content continuity, and accountable ownership.
Establish page-owner and content-reviewer coverage, including rollout communications, enablement, training, and adoption tracking.
Create operating cadences and reporting for migration status, quality, risks, decisions, and executive escalation.

Content Operations and CMS Governance

Define and operate service-level expectations, change controls, quality checks, and governance for ongoing web content operations.
Build repeatable self-service processes, training, and support that enable Product Marketing Managers to manage page updates and edits after WSB migration.
Reduce unnecessary dependence on centralized publishing by clarifying ownership, approval paths, and maintenance expectations.

Website Measurement and KPI Development

Maintain website-performance reporting and operating reviews across traffic, engagement, conversion, and content-performance measures.
Define and track new KPIs, including AI Engine Optimization (AEO), and establish a consistent framework for measuring content and platform impact.
Translate performance insights into prioritized content and website improvements that improve discovery, engagement, and business outcomes.

Oracle AI World Content Operations and Demo Hub Oversight

Own CMS updates for core session titles, abstracts, speakers, and metadata across Learn, Hands-on Labs, Bootcamps, and Theater sessions.
Own the integrated operating plan for Demo Hub content, including content readiness, publishing, AV coordination, on-site updates, and last-minute change management.
Coordinate Demo Hub staffing schedules and train Hub staff on booth-duty expectations and attendee, speaker, and content support.
Track dependencies, staffing coverage, readiness risks, and timely resolution across content, event, and booth stakeholders.

Lead Strategic Programs

Own and drive complex, cross-functional programs that span Product Marketing, Partner, and Product Management organizations, bringing structure and clarity to ambiguous, fast-moving initiatives.
Coordinate concurrent initiatives while maintaining clear priorities, timelines, risks, dependencies, and executive-level status reporting.
Serve as the operational lead for time-sensitive strategic projects, rapidly stepping into high-priority initiatives to accelerate execution.

Responsibilities

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Communications, Marketing, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field or equivalent relevant experience.
6-8+ years of experience in program management, product marketing, technical marketing, product management, web operations, or a related strategic role.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs with multiple stakeholders, competing priorities, and high-visibility deadlines.
Strong operational judgment and the ability to establish governance, operating cadences, clear accountability, and practical decision-making mechanisms.
Experience with CMS or website operations, content lifecycle management, and web analytics; familiarity with migration, publishing, and quality-assurance workflows.
Exceptional organizational and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence without authority and maintain high quality in fast-paced environments.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in cloud infrastructure, enterprise software, AI, or a large-scale digital property.
Experience defining performance metrics or operating reviews for content, web, digital marketing, or customer experience programs.
Experience supporting a major event, content program, or other time-sensitive field operation.

Successful candidates will:

Create a durable operating model that enables consistent website migration, content governance, ownership coverage, and self-service publishing.
Use measurement and AEO insights to identify high-value improvements and demonstrate the impact of website and content investments.
Deliver a coordinated, well-staffed, and responsive Oracle AI World Demo Hub and content operation.
Create alignment across diverse stakeholders while navigating ambiguity, changing priorities, and time-sensitive business needs.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
BAE Systems Digital Intelligence is home to 4,500 digital, cyber and intelligence experts. We work collaboratively across 10 countries to collect, connect and understand complex data, so that governments, nation states, armed forces and commercial businesses can unlock digital advantage in the most demanding environments.

The Digital Intelligence division of BAE Systems delivers solutions which protect and enhance the connected world. Everything we do creates a safer future. We help nations, governments and businesses around the world defend themselves against cybercrime, reduce their risk in the connected world, comply with regulation, and transform their operations. We do this using our unique set of solutions, expertise and experience.

You will be involved in shaping, mobilising, planning and leading critical projects for key National Security, Defence and Telecommunications. The role requires you to hold an active NV2 clearance at the time of commencement.

Role Summary

We’re looking to hire a Project manager in to our project delivery team focusing on a diverse and ever-changing portfolio of projects within our National Security and Defence business areas based in Canberra.

As a Project manager, you will manage a small project, or a part of a larger, more complex project, (such as a particular work package), or will support a Program Managerwith aspects of managing a larger project.

At this level the incumbent may lead a small team of professional staff, being responsible for managing their delivery and performance and providing appraisal and support to their development.

They will have a level of experience in one or more areas of PM practice and be expected to be able to adapt and apply these practices in different circumstances, to develop these practices and to guide and instruct others in their application.

Role Description

Core Duties:

Able to perform advanced project reporting & scheduling.
Able to undertake advanced problem solving typically based on previous experience.
Have a comprehensive knowledge of Business process and procedures.
Administration and general office skills including spreadsheets/ Microsoft packages.
Attend on the job training as appropriate.
Able to lead a small project or a work package of a larger project.
Able to manage the full project lifecycle to ensure that, over time, the needs of customers/users continue to be met and that financial and other benefits are achieved.
Identify, assesses and manages risks to the success of the project. Applies appropriate PM methods and tools whether predictive (plan-driven) approaches or adaptive (iterative/agile) approaches. Agrees project approach with stakeholders, and prepares realistic plans (including quality, risk and communications plans) and tracks activities against the project schedule, managing stakeholder involvement as appropriate.
Consolidate expertise from multiple sources, including third party experts, to provide coherent advice to further organisational objectives. Supports and promotes the development and sharing of specialist knowledge within the organisation.
This is a role for an experienced project professional with a small team and the ability to deliver with limited guidance from the Line Manager.
Deputises for the Project Manager as appropriate.

Knowledge, Skills And Qualifications

Comprehensive knowledge and understanding of PM policies, processes, procedures and systems.
Comprehensive PM experience demonstrated in a professional capacity and the specialist skills to ensure procedures are followed with the ability to define the standards which the others will operate. Guides others in application of Project Management processes.
Comprehensive knowledge and understanding of their project.
Comprehensive understanding of one or more Project Management tools techniques and practices.
Comprehensive knowledge and understanding of the Business environment for their project.
Good knowledge and experience of PM governance and assurance processes such as Integrated Baseline Reviews (IBRs). Typically an Assessor for LCM Reviews.
Strong experience of influencing stakeholders both inside and outside the company.
Comprehensive understanding of the wider PM environment, and of developments and practices in the field.
Comprehensive understanding of own project/s, its markets, customers, strategic priorities and culture.
Knowledge acquired through job related training and on the job experience with theoretical and practical skills.
Experience of building relationships and negotiating outcomes with internal stakeholders.
Gathers and analyses information. Supports development of solutions and of implementation approaches.

Skills

Applies problem solving techniques to situations of moderate complexity in the field of PM, taking requirements and data from internal (project) sources and external (customer, competitor and academic) areas.
A comprehensive understanding of how team integrates with others teams & projects in order to achieve objectives.
Quality and timeliness of work reflects on the effectiveness of the immediate team. Business acumen that goes beyond immediate team.
Make judgments, recommendations and advises on analysis of factual information.
Impact in terms of providing services/information on matters that assist others in controlling or making decisions.
Communication exchange can be complex and could involve sensitive information.

Qualifications

Application of related PM Competencies will be expected at this level.
Roles typically require a University Degree, or a substantial amount of practical knowledge gained through experience.
Incumbent may have a PM Qualification such as the APM Project Management Qualification.

Learn more about us & our benefits:
https://www.baesystems.com/en/digital/careers/our-locations/asia-pacific/australia

Head Office Near CBD

Our client is a well established commercial construction company with a strong project portfolio and a reputation for quality delivery. They are seeking an experienced Senior Project Manager to join their Senior Leadership Team and take accountability for the operational performance and successful delivery of their construction projects.

This is a genuine leadership opportunity for a construction professional who wants to shape strategy, build high performing teams and drive outcomes across a diverse project pipeline, rather than simply managing a single job at a time.

About The Role

Reporting to the Director, the Senior Project Manager provides leadership, direction and oversight across design management, project planning and construction delivery, ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently, on time and within approved commercial parameters. You will maintain visibility across all active projects, identify emerging risks early and step in where needed to protect project outcomes and keep delivery moving.

As a key member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will also contribute to company strategy, project pipeline planning, operational improvement and the long-term growth of the business.

Oversee end to end delivery of the project portfolio, holding Project Managers and project teams accountable for outcomes, reporting and company standards
Maintain oversight of commercial and financial performance, including margin, cash flow, procurement, variations and claims
Provide oversight of head contracts, subcontracts and supplier agreements, acting as the key escalation point for contractual and commercial matters
Drive early identification and management of construction, design, commercial and operational risk, and monitor WHSEQ performance across the portfolio
Lead, mentor and develop Project Managers and project delivery teams, building capable and collaborative teams
Maintain strong relationships with clients, consultants and subcontractors, acting as a senior escalation point on major projects
Prepare and present monthly portfolio performance reporting to the Senior Leadership Team

About You

Minimum 10 years' relevant experience in commercial construction
Tertiary qualifications in Construction Management, Engineering or a related discipline
Proven experience as a Senior Project Manager, Project Director, Construction Manager or Operations Manager with a commercial construction head contractor
Demonstrated experience overseeing multiple projects and project teams concurrently
Strong commercial acumen across budgets, forecasting, procurement, variations and contractual risk
A practical, visible leadership style with a willingness to attend sites and support your teams
Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills
Experience working within ISO-certified quality, safety and environmental systems
Proficiency in construction management and programming systems such as Procore, HammerTech, Jobpac, Microsoft Office and Microsoft Project (or comparable platforms)
Current Australian driver licence and General Construction Induction Card

WHY APPLY

This is an opportunity to take a senior leadership role with genuine influence over strategy, culture and project outcomes, within a business that values accountability, integrity and high performance. You will have the autonomy to shape how projects are delivered and the support of a collaborative leadership team to back you.

PROJECT MANAGER

Job Description

ABOUT US

Established in 1979, Leed Electric, Inc. has made its mark on the construction industry by providing the highest quality electrical and technology systems. We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including medical benefits, paid time off, retirement plan options, and other employee benefits.

Summary

The Project Manager is responsible for the overall direction, completion, and financial outcome for several concurrent projects, from pre-construction to closeouts. The PM leads and manages a team of assistant project managers, project engineers and office engineers to deliver exceptional results. The Project Manager supports client relationships and participates in business development activities as appropriate. Reports to the Division Manager.

Position Responsibilities

Establish project objectives, procedures, and performance standards consistent with company policies and contractual requirements. Put these in clear concise work statement for the field.
Complete Job Information Sheet (JIS) and Project Budget.
Accountable for overall profit and performance of the project.
Supervise and provide direction to project management staff, including Assistant Project Managers, Project Engineers, and Project Coordinators.
Train and effectively supervise direct reports in the company philosophy and systems.
Review drawings for questions or changes to be submitted via RFI. Review RFI’s received from vendors and subcontractors.
Negotiate and supervise the preparation of all change orders on the project.
Develop cost and billing projections and project Schedule of Values (SOV).
Maintain liaison with prime client and A/E to facilitate construction activities.
Monitor construction activities in conjunction with the onsite Foreman and Division Superintendent to ensure project is being built on schedule, and within budgets.
Manage subcontractor activities including associated costs, schedule, and related change orders.
Identify project issues and implement corrective actions consistent with company policies and in coordination with the Division Manager.
Represent company/project in meetings with client, subcontractors, etc.
Engage in business development.
Manage financial aspects of contracts (progress billing, rental equipment, income/expenses) to protect the company’s interest and simultaneously maintain a good relationship with the client.
This position may require occasional travel to project sites, client meetings, and company locations within the assigned region.
Perform other duties as assigned by Division Manager.

Education, Certification, Skills And/Or Abilities Required

Minimum Experience: Minimum 8–10 years of progressive project management experience in electrical construction or a related construction discipline.

Education: Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Electrical Engineering, Structural Engineering, or related discipline preferred; equivalent combination of education, training, and experience considered.

Certifications: Valid California Driver’s License required. OSHA 10 certification preferred or ability to obtain within a reasonable timeframe.

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000 (exempt) annually. The actual base salary offered will depend on factors including, but not limited to, experience, qualifications, skills, education, certifications, geographic location, and internal equity.

Abilities Required

Industry

Knowledge of construction technology, cost management, scheduling, equipment, and methods required.
Advanced abilities in reading and interpreting plans and specifications.
In-depth knowledge of the NFPA/NEC codes.
Extensive knowledge of safety protocols and procedures.
Basic understanding of California Construction Law and claims avoidance principles
Extensive experience managing electrical construction projects.
Knowledge of applicable federal, state, and local construction regulations, including OSHA requirements and California labor compliance requirements.

Business

Proficient in using a computer and Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, etc.).
Bluebeam skills (CAD and BIM) as well as Accubid and Procore a plus.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks, changing priorities as necessary.
Ability to work under time pressure and adapt to changing requirements with a positive attitude.
Problem-solving skills with a proven ability to exercise initiative, judgment, and discretion.
Understanding of the financials of a project and how to forecast.

Interpersonal

Excellent leadership and people management skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate a high-performing team.
Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build strong relationships and negotiate effectively with team members, customers, consultants, vendors, and partners.
Business development / heavy client interaction.
Strong verbal and written communication skills necessary to effectively communicate with clients, subcontractors, vendors, employees, and project stakeholders by telephone, email, and other communication methods. Regular telephone communication with customers and business contacts is an essential part of the position.

WORKING CONDITIONS

Work is conducted primarily indoors with varying environmental conditions such as fluorescent lighting and air conditioning. May be sitting for long periods, standing, walking, typing, carrying, pushing, and bending. At a job site, may be exposed to potentially hazardous conditions.
The noise level is usually low to medium; it can be loud on a jobsite.
We fully comply with the ADA and applicable state law, including considering reasonable accommodation measures that may enable qualified disabled applicants and employees to perform essential functions.
Ability to occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds with or without reasonable accommodation.

jobs.description:
Role Overview

This is a site-embedded SME role focused on the specific ELV, BMS, and security infrastructure of a designated data centre campus or facility. Unlike the portfolio-level SME role, this position requires deep, facility-specific technical knowledge — the as-built configuration, site-specific control logic, vendor systems in use, and local operational constraints of the assigned site — to provide hands-on technical support to site operations, construction, and commissioning teams.

Key Responsibilities

Act as the on-site/site-dedicated technical point of contact for all ELV, BMS, and security system matters at the assigned facility.
Maintain detailed, current knowledge of the site's as-built ELV and BMS architecture, including device inventory, network topology, controller configurations, and integration points with EPMS and fire/life-safety systems.
Support live-site troubleshooting of ELV, BMS, and security system faults, coordinating with OEM vendors and facility operations/NOC teams for rapid resolution.
Review and validate site-specific change requests (MOPs/EOPs) affecting ELV, BMS, or security systems before implementation.
Provide technical walkdown support during audits, client inspections, and compliance reviews specific to the site.
Support site commissioning and re-commissioning activities for ELV, BMS, and security systems during capacity expansions, retrofits, or system upgrades.
Maintain and update site-specific documentation — as-built drawings, points lists, network diagrams, and system configuration baselines — reflecting all field changes.
Coordinate with the portfolio-level ELV & Security SME on design standard alignment, escalations, and lessons learned across sites.
Support incident response and root-cause investigations for site-specific ELV/BMS/security events, including data gathering, log review, and vendor coordination.
Train and guide site facility/operations personnel on ELV and BMS system operation, alarm handling, and basic troubleshooting.

Required Skills & Experience

8–12 years of experience in ELV and BMS systems, with demonstrated experience providing hands-on, site-level technical support in a live/operational data centre environment.
Working knowledge of the specific BMS/EPMS platform(s) deployed at the assigned site (e.g., Niagara/Tridium, Schneider EcoStruxure, Siemens Desigo, Honeywell, Johnson Controls Metasys).
Practical experience with CCTV, access control, intrusion detection, and PA systems as deployed and configured on an operational site.
Familiarity with MOP/EOP (Method of Procedure / Emergency Operating Procedure) development and change control processes in a live critical facility.
Ability to interpret as-built drawings, control narratives, and network diagrams specific to the site, and to identify discrepancies against current field conditions.
Comfort working in a 24x7 critical facility environment, including responding to on-call escalations as required.
Strong troubleshooting mindset with the ability to work directly with OEM technical support and field service engineers.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical/Electronics/Instrumentation Engineering, or related field, or equivalent hands-on field experience.
Site-specific OEM training/certification on the BMS or security platforms deployed at the facility.
Prior experience in a site operations, facility engineering, or critical environment support role.

Soft Skills

Strong ownership mindset and responsiveness in live-site, time-sensitive situations.
Clear, concise communication with site operations, NOC, and vendor teams during incidents.
Ability to work independently on site while staying aligned with portfolio-level design standards and reporting lines.

Spektrum supports apex purchasers (NATO, UN, EU and National Government and Defence) and their Tier 1 supplier ecosystem with a wide range of specialist services. We provide our clients with professional services, specialised aerospace and defence sales, delivery, and operational subject matter expertise. We are looking for personnel to join our team and support key client projects.
Who we are supporting

Allied Command Transformation (ACT)
is NATO’s leading agent for change: driving, facilitating, and advocating the continuous improvement of Alliance capabilities to maintain and enhance the military relevance and effectiveness of the Alliance. The main objectives of ACT are: providing appropriate support to NATO missions and operations; leading NATO military transformation; and improving relationships, interaction and practical cooperation with partners, nations and international organisations. ACT therefore leads Alliance concept development, capability development, training and lessons-learned initiatives and provides unfettered military support to policy development within NATO.
The program 

Capability Development & Management Support (CDMS)

DCOS Capability Development (CAPDEV)
acts as the Supreme Allied Commander Transformation's Director for guidance, direction and coordination of the activities and resources of the Capability Development Directorate.
The Requirements Division
will execute all tasks and activities needed to support requirements management for NATO capabilities
The Capability Requirements (CR)
Branch will develop the Capability Requirements Brief and recommended courses of action to resolve issues through the life cycle management of requirements using matrixed, cross-functional project-specific Requirements Management teams.
The Requirements Forward Branch (Mons)
is responsible for conducting requirements development and management representation and engagement-related functions in Europe.
The Capability Division
coordinates the development of capabilities from capability planning through acceptance and then disposal with management entities, NATO Headquarters staff and the NATO Governance Structure
The Capability Forward Branch (Mons)
coordinates with ACO, NCIA, NSPA, NATO HQ, territorial Host Nations, and NATO Centres of Excellence (COEs) to support the development of capabilities.
Strategic Plans and Policy (SPP)
supports Allied Command Transformation in formalizing military advice to shape future military strategy, political guidance, and other policy documents supporting NATO’s strategic objectives.
Role ID: ACT-CDMS-27-01-A-LC11

Role and Duties

The Operational Analysis Branch provides analysts to capability development programme teams to drive and support evidence-based decision making in requirements derivation and programmatic planning. In this SOW, “Operational Analysis” (predominantly military term) is used interchangeably with “Operations Research” (US term) and “Operational Research” (UK Term).
Course of Action (COA) analysis supports capability development programme teams to determine appropriate DOTMLPFI methods and capability architectures for meeting the military user’s operational requirements and defining programmatic structures.
Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) involves the comparative assessment of options in terms of costs, risks, schedules and operational effectiveness. The AoA tests the commercial marketplace and NATO’s ability to re-use capabilities that are in service in member Nations militaries. It establishes whether NATO should procure a managed service, adopt National capability solutions, acquire products from industry, or must develop bespoke solutions. For complex programmes, the AoA can inform programmatic structures by showing how value for money is most likely to be achieved.
NATO capability development decisions concern complex socio-technical systems, including computer information systems supporting NATO command and control, federated governance arrangements, capability integration activities and multinational delivery models. Analysts must be capable of combining quantitative and qualitative evidence and facilitating stakeholder engagement to support defensible decision-making. COA analysis and AoA typically involves engaging with the programme team to understand programmatic areas of uncertainty, designing and facilitating workshops to gather stakeholder views (including within the military NATO Command Structure, delivery Agencies and Centres of Excellence and / or the NATO Force Structure, gathering or generating (if appropriate) cost, risk schedule and effectiveness evidence, and comparative options assessment. This may include the development or elicitation of Measures of Performance (MoPs) and Measures of Effectiveness (MoEs); assessment of absolute and comparative risks; elicitation of schedule estimates; and review of cost estimates for appropriateness to support this assessment.
Operations Research methods can be applied at any stage of the capability development programme, including, but not limited to: decision science (e.g. multi-criteria decision analysis), optimization (e.g. linear programming), modelling & simulation, behavioural operations research, data science (e.g. advanced analytics and machine learning) and wargaming.
Taskings:

Contribute to Course of Action analysis using Operations Research and Analysis methods in support of Capability Development within ACT in order to mature NATO capability requirements and set programmatic direction.
Plan and conduct research to study and establish qualitative and quantitative assessments of operational effectiveness, undertake cost-effectiveness and risk-benefit studies and analyses.
Where necessary and appropriate, interact with NATO and National research entities and industries to establish the impact of alternatives on operational effectiveness.
Where necessary and appropriate, attend engagements or workshops with NATO, National organizations, and / or industry to ensure cost estimation activities are likely to provide outputs of appropriate quality to support analysis.
Support the creation of Requests for Information and surveys to NATO Nations, Non Governmental Organizations, and industry.
Analyse the potential impact of identified individual and aggregated risks, and propose possible risk management approaches.
Elicit, and / or review and assess schedule estimates, to ensure appropriate quality and supporting evidence for decisions being supported by analysis.
Review and assess cost estimates provided by others, to ensure appropriate quality and supporting evidence for decisions being supported by analysis.
Analyse and document comparative assessments of cost, risk, schedule and operational effectiveness to inform programmatic decision-making.
Produce decision briefs / presentations describing the underlying rationale / justification for analytical outcomes. If appropriate, brief decision-makers on the context, process and outcomes.
Produce written reports of analysis conducted as part of the Capability Programme plan evidence package, for review with the International Military Staff and International Staff in NATO Headquarters.
Produce summary briefs of lessons identified / lessons learned to support continuous improvement of NATO capability development and OA branch skills and competencies.
May be required to travel to meetings and conferences both within and outside NATO boundaries for up to 60 days per year.

Essential Qualifications

Who We Are Looking For

We are looking for Integrated Audit Data Analyst, Officer to join the Corporate Audit Team. Corporate Audit conducts internal audits of all of State Street’s business lines, including Investment Services, Global Markets, Global Advisors, and corporate functions. In this position, you will play a data specialist role as part of dynamic and cross functional teams responsible for the execution of individual audit engagements. In this role, you will work under the direction of audit project lead to support the execution of the audit through the use of data analytics. This will require both audit skills, as well as an understanding of data analytics, to allow the auditor to interface with business partners, execute control design assessments and operational effectiveness testing, developing audit test conclusions and drafting summary observations. The Integrated Data Analyst will partner with both the Data Analytics team and the business audit team to design data-driven test approaches in audit projects. You will also work with the business audit teams to analyze the results of data analytic control tests to identify potential control weaknesses. You will also play a role in the onboarding and coaching of junior staff and support various departmental initiatives.

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining plays an important role in the overall success of the organization. Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability; regulators rely upon us to provide assurance that the bank operates in a manner that is compliant with key banking regulations to properly manage risks to the company and the global financial systems. To make that happen we need teams like yours to help navigate employees and the organization as a whole. In your role, you will help us build resilience and execute day to day deliverables at our best. Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As an Integrated Data Analyst, Officer you will:

Leverage data analytics skills to perform audit work in line with the Division’s risk-based methodology and the Institute of Internal Auditor’s standards to identify and understand risk; determine control objectives; and evaluate whether controls sufficiently address identified risks through various data analysis techniques.
Serve as a conduit between the Business Audit Team and the Data Analytics Team to ensure an understanding of business processes and data analytics capabilities, to drive better data analytics outcomes, including the establishment of repeatable data analytics/continuous auditing use cases.
Obtain and analyze evidentiary data as a basis for drafting informed and objective opinions on the adequacy and effectives of controls under review. This may include previously identified data analytics approaches; however, the Integrated Data Analyst will be expected to leverage their data analytics knowledge to partner with the central Data Analytics team and the business audit team to design enhanced analytics approaches.
Draft audit issues that clearly outline the identified issue and underlying root cause, using data analysis to support conclusions and inferences regarding risk of findings.
Review corrective actions taken by management to improve deficient conditions.
Escalate potential issues / obstacles to audit management along with proposed solutions.
Develop and maintain understanding of internal State Street products and processes, relevant industry and regulatory topics, and data analytics best practices.
Develop an understanding of State Street data constructs, systems, and processes, to better position the team for more effective data analytics-based auditing.
Develop relationships with audit clients and business partners across the lines of defense; serve as the primary audit contact for assigned area in individual audit engagements.
Contribute to change initiatives through active participation in working groups and adoption of practices in day-to-day responsibilities.
Share successes and challenges with peer Integrated Data Analysts and the Data Analytics Team to increase the future success of the Data Analytics program.
Assist in the onboarding of audit staff, and the coaching of business auditors in the use of data analytics.

These skills will help you succeed in this role

The ability to operate in a complex, non-routine and fast-paced environment that requires working independently and as part of a team.
Strong technical ability in AI and data science.
Strong technical ability in data analysis and control testing
Ability to clearly demonstrate proficiency in evaluating business processes, identifying inherent risk and testing associated internal controls.
A high degree of professionalism and proficient organizational, analytical, problem solving and project management skills.
Excellent communication (written and verbal), interpersonal and presentation skills
Proven ability to research, interpret and apply regulatory requirements.

Advanced degree or certification (CFA, FRM, CPA, CIA) preferrable.
Technical expertise with Databricks is preferrable.
Experience in auditing information technology general controls.

While majority of the time you will work from your primary location, some domestic and international travel may be required to a variety of locations where State Street operates.

We truly believe in the power that comes from the diverse backgrounds and experiences our employees bring with them. About PILLAR:

PILLAR (formerly Ringkas) builds AI-native infrastructure for financial institutions. We started in 2022 as Southeast Asia's embedded mortgage platform and now run the AI layer banks use to originate, qualify, and convert lending customers.

The role:

Our AI engineering team runs the agent. You're the analytical brain behind it — sharpening the frameworks for each customer segment, extracting insight from growing volumes of conversation data, and improving how the agent reads and responds to each type of customer.
You'll also own product and business analytics with the Head of Product: instrumentation, experiments, dashboards, and the analysis that decides what we build next.

What you'll do:

Sit in product reviews before engineering starts, and turn product goals into metric specs — what's trackable, what isn't, flagged before code is written.
Keep behavioral analytics honest: validate events, find the gaps, write the spec that fixes them.
Write complex SQL against raw tables, and build dashboards the team uses without asking you.
Run experiments end to end — size them, read them, and say clearly when a result is inconclusive.
Turn patterns in retention, drop-off, and adoption into a recommendation someone can act on.
Build scoring models that feed the product directly: lead propensity, drop-off prediction, match quality.
Design evaluation for our AI Agent — offline eval sets, LLM-as-judge calibration, and the call on whether a regression is real or noise.

What we require:

We hire for reasoning ability, not resume length.
Recent graduates and people with five years of experience are evaluated the same way.
A genuine statistics foundation.
What a p-value actually means, why a result can be significant and useless, how you'd size a test.
Structuring ability.
Given an ambiguous question, you decompose it, decide what's worth measuring, and defend your approach. This is what we screen hardest for.
Clear communication.
You'll write for banks and executives — an analysis nobody understands is worth nothing.
Real SQL.
Window functions, debugging a join that's silently duplicating rows, working against raw tables. We test this.
Python
— pandas for cohort work, and enough statistics libraries to run a test properly.
Daily use of AI tools
in real work.
English and Bahasa Indonesia.

About the Role:

We are seeking a Program Manager to support the Energy and Sustainability organization’s clean energy strategy and the reporting that underpins Net Zero commitments.
The role will serve as the day-to-day owner and coordinator for energy activity data — the Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 energy datasets that feed the company's greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory, emissions forecasting, and voluntary and regulatory disclosures.
This is a hands-on, data-centric role requiring 3-5 years of experience managing multiple concurrent workstreams in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, direct experience working with large datasets and running or Quality Checking (QC'ing) analytics, and the ability to communicate data status and insights to technical and non-technical audiences.
The individual must have familiarity with corporate GHG accounting and be comfortable with query tools and data Quality Assurance (QA)/validation workflows.

Job Title:
Sustainability Program Manager II
Minimum Qualifications:

BA or BS degree in physical sciences, engineering, math, statistics, accounting, business, environment, and/or a sustainability-focused field.
3-5 years of experience in program management, data operations, or analytics coordination, ideally supporting technical or data-oriented teams.
Direct, hands-on experience working with large datasets — collecting, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), reconciling, and analyzing data from multiple sources.
Familiarity with corporate Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions accounting concepts (Scope 1, 2, and 3) and the activity data that underpins an emissions inventory.
Exceptional project-management skills with a demonstrated ability to self-manage complex, data-driven delivery in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience presenting data and insights to technical and non-technical audiences and creating graphics for leadership presentations.
Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data work, even under tight deadlines.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment and comfort with ambiguity.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience with a scripting/query language (e.g., Structured Query Language (SQL), Python) sufficient to run, automate, or Quality Assurance (QA) data pulls from large data warehouses (e.g., Hive/Presto or equivalent).
Experience building visualizations and dashboards from large, multi-source datasets, particularly with Tableau and Excel.
Familiarity with energy/utility data (electricity, natural gas, diesel, and other fuels) and metering/billing data structures.
Strong understanding of current practices and trends in greenhouse gas emissions and broader sustainability accounting and reporting.
Familiarity with external reporting standards and platforms such as Greenhouse Gas Protocol (GHGP), Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB), Global Reporting Initiative (GRI), Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB), Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), etc.
Experience supporting external assurance or audit processes.

Key Responsibilities:

Serve as the day-to-day owner for energy activity data across Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 electricity (e.g., FERA, construction energy, network-related electricity, and operational electricity, diesel, natural gas, etc.), from data collection and Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) through to the reporting handoff to the Net Zero team.
Perform analyses on the Environmental Attribute Certificate (EAC) portfolio and support the development of internal systems to advance portfolio management and modeling.
Run and maintain the recurring data collection, Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC), and validation cadence (e.g., quarterly data pulls, follow-ups, Year-over-Year (YoY) analysis) and keep reporting and analysis on schedule.
Perform and Quality Check (QC) data pulls from energy data systems, investigate anomalies and data-pipeline issues, and reconcile discrepancies.
Coordinate data and process flows across cross-functional partners to maintain accurate and complete inputs from source through to reporting.
Support the emissions forecasting cadence as the energy-data point of contact for the Net Zero team, providing and Quality Assuring (QA'ing) the activity data behind regulatory and internal cross-functional forecasts.
Develop and maintain program-management artifacts — trackers, roadmaps, status reports, and executive-ready updates — for recurring leadership and cross-functional forums.
Support a quarterly reporting cadence (execution updates, executive meeting preparation, deck and dashboard creation) using established templates and inputs.
Support external assurance and audit activities (e.g., methodology walkthroughs with the assurance provider) and prepare and validate data and documentation as requested.
Triage and respond to incoming energy-data and analytical requests; track progress against internal Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and stakeholder expectations.
Maintain and improve reporting documentation — the what, when, where, how, and why of energy data collection, including team-specific nuances and process flows.

We’re looking to hire a Project manager in to our project delivery team focusing on a diverse and ever-changing portfolio of projects within our National Security and Defence business areas based in Canberra.

As a Project manager, you will manage a small project, or a part of a larger, more complex project, (such as a particular work package), or will support a Program Managerwith aspects of managing a larger project.

new_jobs.description:
Role Overview

This is a site-embedded SME role focused on the specific ELV, BMS, and security infrastructure of a designated data centre campus or facility. Unlike the portfolio-level SME role, this position requires deep, facility-specific technical knowledge — the as-built configuration, site-specific control logic, vendor systems in use, and local operational constraints of the assigned site — to provide hands-on technical support to site operations, construction, and commissioning teams.

Key Responsibilities

Act as the on-site/site-dedicated technical point of contact for all ELV, BMS, and security system matters at the assigned facility.
Maintain detailed, current knowledge of the site's as-built ELV and BMS architecture, including device inventory, network topology, controller configurations, and integration points with EPMS and fire/life-safety systems.
Support live-site troubleshooting of ELV, BMS, and security system faults, coordinating with OEM vendors and facility operations/NOC teams for rapid resolution.
Review and validate site-specific change requests (MOPs/EOPs) affecting ELV, BMS, or security systems before implementation.
Provide technical walkdown support during audits, client inspections, and compliance reviews specific to the site.
Support site commissioning and re-commissioning activities for ELV, BMS, and security systems during capacity expansions, retrofits, or system upgrades.
Maintain and update site-specific documentation — as-built drawings, points lists, network diagrams, and system configuration baselines — reflecting all field changes.
Coordinate with the portfolio-level ELV & Security SME on design standard alignment, escalations, and lessons learned across sites.
Support incident response and root-cause investigations for site-specific ELV/BMS/security events, including data gathering, log review, and vendor coordination.
Train and guide site facility/operations personnel on ELV and BMS system operation, alarm handling, and basic troubleshooting.

Required Skills & Experience

8–12 years of experience in ELV and BMS systems, with demonstrated experience providing hands-on, site-level technical support in a live/operational data centre environment.
Working knowledge of the specific BMS/EPMS platform(s) deployed at the assigned site (e.g., Niagara/Tridium, Schneider EcoStruxure, Siemens Desigo, Honeywell, Johnson Controls Metasys).
Practical experience with CCTV, access control, intrusion detection, and PA systems as deployed and configured on an operational site.
Familiarity with MOP/EOP (Method of Procedure / Emergency Operating Procedure) development and change control processes in a live critical facility.
Ability to interpret as-built drawings, control narratives, and network diagrams specific to the site, and to identify discrepancies against current field conditions.
Comfort working in a 24x7 critical facility environment, including responding to on-call escalations as required.
Strong troubleshooting mindset with the ability to work directly with OEM technical support and field service engineers.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Electrical/Electronics/Instrumentation Engineering, or related field, or equivalent hands-on field experience.
Site-specific OEM training/certification on the BMS or security platforms deployed at the facility.
Prior experience in a site operations, facility engineering, or critical environment support role.

Soft Skills

Strong ownership mindset and responsiveness in live-site, time-sensitive situations.
Clear, concise communication with site operations, NOC, and vendor teams during incidents.
Ability to work independently on site while staying aligned with portfolio-level design standards and reporting lines.

is responsible for conducting requirements development and management representation and engagement-related functions in Europe.
The Capability Division
coordinates the development of capabilities from capability planning through acceptance and then disposal with management entities, NATO Headquarters staff and the NATO Governance Structure
The Capability Forward Branch (Mons)
coordinates with ACO, NCIA, NSPA, NATO HQ, territorial Host Nations, and NATO Centres of Excellence (COEs) to support the development of capabilities.
Strategic Plans and Policy (SPP)
supports Allied Command Transformation in formalizing military advice to shape future military strategy, political guidance, and other policy documents supporting NATO’s strategic objectives.
Role ID: ACT-CDMS-27-01-A-LC11

Role and Duties

The Operational Analysis Branch provides analysts to capability development programme teams to drive and support evidence-based decision making in requirements derivation and programmatic planning. In this SOW, “Operational Analysis” (predominantly military term) is used interchangeably with “Operations Research” (US term) and “Operational Research” (UK Term).
Course of Action (COA) analysis supports capability development programme teams to determine appropriate DOTMLPFI methods and capability architectures for meeting the military user’s operational requirements and defining programmatic structures.
Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) involves the comparative assessment of options in terms of costs, risks, schedules and operational effectiveness. The AoA tests the commercial marketplace and NATO’s ability to re-use capabilities that are in service in member Nations militaries. It establishes whether NATO should procure a managed service, adopt National capability solutions, acquire products from industry, or must develop bespoke solutions. For complex programmes, the AoA can inform programmatic structures by showing how value for money is most likely to be achieved.
NATO capability development decisions concern complex socio-technical systems, including computer information systems supporting NATO command and control, federated governance arrangements, capability integration activities and multinational delivery models. Analysts must be capable of combining quantitative and qualitative evidence and facilitating stakeholder engagement to support defensible decision-making. COA analysis and AoA typically involves engaging with the programme team to understand programmatic areas of uncertainty, designing and facilitating workshops to gather stakeholder views (including within the military NATO Command Structure, delivery Agencies and Centres of Excellence and / or the NATO Force Structure, gathering or generating (if appropriate) cost, risk schedule and effectiveness evidence, and comparative options assessment. This may include the development or elicitation of Measures of Performance (MoPs) and Measures of Effectiveness (MoEs); assessment of absolute and comparative risks; elicitation of schedule estimates; and review of cost estimates for appropriateness to support this assessment.
Operations Research methods can be applied at any stage of the capability development programme, including, but not limited to: decision science (e.g. multi-criteria decision analysis), optimization (e.g. linear programming), modelling & simulation, behavioural operations research, data science (e.g. advanced analytics and machine learning) and wargaming.
Taskings:

Contribute to Course of Action analysis using Operations Research and Analysis methods in support of Capability Development within ACT in order to mature NATO capability requirements and set programmatic direction.
Plan and conduct research to study and establish qualitative and quantitative assessments of operational effectiveness, undertake cost-effectiveness and risk-benefit studies and analyses.
Where necessary and appropriate, interact with NATO and National research entities and industries to establish the impact of alternatives on operational effectiveness.
Where necessary and appropriate, attend engagements or workshops with NATO, National organizations, and / or industry to ensure cost estimation activities are likely to provide outputs of appropriate quality to support analysis.
Support the creation of Requests for Information and surveys to NATO Nations, Non Governmental Organizations, and industry.
Analyse the potential impact of identified individual and aggregated risks, and propose possible risk management approaches.
Elicit, and / or review and assess schedule estimates, to ensure appropriate quality and supporting evidence for decisions being supported by analysis.
Review and assess cost estimates provided by others, to ensure appropriate quality and supporting evidence for decisions being supported by analysis.
Analyse and document comparative assessments of cost, risk, schedule and operational effectiveness to inform programmatic decision-making.
Produce decision briefs / presentations describing the underlying rationale / justification for analytical outcomes. If appropriate, brief decision-makers on the context, process and outcomes.
Produce written reports of analysis conducted as part of the Capability Programme plan evidence package, for review with the International Military Staff and International Staff in NATO Headquarters.
Produce summary briefs of lessons identified / lessons learned to support continuous improvement of NATO capability development and OA branch skills and competencies.
May be required to travel to meetings and conferences both within and outside NATO boundaries for up to 60 days per year.
Perform additional tasks as required by the COTR related to the LABOR category.

Essential Qualifications

A Bachelor’s degree in Operations Research, Mathematics, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering or equivalent quantitative degree. Alternatively, 5+ years of Operations Research/ Operational Analysis experience conducting and leading analytical studies in relevant military, strategic, political or international environment.NATO UNCLASSIFIED

With a relevant Bachelor’s degree (listed above), only 2 years in the last 5 must be in the fields / areas /listed above.
Experience designing, leading, and facilitating structured stakeholder engagements to elicit objectives, assumptions, measures, risks, preferences and expert judgement in support of defence capability decisions involving technical and non-technical stakeholders across multiple levels of seniority.
Experience, within last 5 years of determining Operations Research / Operational Analysis requirements, scoping problems for study, developing analysis plans, and delivering highquality outputs that influence senior decision makers.

About PILLAR:

PILLAR (formerly Ringkas) builds AI-native infrastructure for financial institutions. We started in 2022 as Southeast Asia's embedded mortgage platform and now run the AI layer banks use to originate, qualify, and convert lending customers.

The role:

Our AI engineering team runs the agent. You're the analytical brain behind it — sharpening the frameworks for each customer segment, extracting insight from growing volumes of conversation data, and improving how the agent reads and responds to each type of customer.
You'll also own product and business analytics with the Head of Product: instrumentation, experiments, dashboards, and the analysis that decides what we build next.

What you'll do:

Sit in product reviews before engineering starts, and turn product goals into metric specs — what's trackable, what isn't, flagged before code is written.
Keep behavioral analytics honest: validate events, find the gaps, write the spec that fixes them.
Write complex SQL against raw tables, and build dashboards the team uses without asking you.
Run experiments end to end — size them, read them, and say clearly when a result is inconclusive.
Turn patterns in retention, drop-off, and adoption into a recommendation someone can act on.
Build scoring models that feed the product directly: lead propensity, drop-off prediction, match quality.
Design evaluation for our AI Agent — offline eval sets, LLM-as-judge calibration, and the call on whether a regression is real or noise.

What we require:

We hire for reasoning ability, not resume length.
Recent graduates and people with five years of experience are evaluated the same way.
A genuine statistics foundation.
What a p-value actually means, why a result can be significant and useless, how you'd size a test.
Structuring ability.
Given an ambiguous question, you decompose it, decide what's worth measuring, and defend your approach. This is what we screen hardest for.
Clear communication.
You'll write for banks and executives — an analysis nobody understands is worth nothing.
Real SQL.
Window functions, debugging a join that's silently duplicating rows, working against raw tables. We test this.
Python
— pandas for cohort work, and enough statistics libraries to run a test properly.
Daily use of AI tools
in real work.
English and Bahasa Indonesia.
Arabic is a plus — our conversation data is multilingual.
